# Structural check of the causal argument. Ranking "most" is interpretive, so it is reported as UNSUPPORTED.

# Claim: wearing less on cold, overcast days causes arthritis.
# A counterexample to a causal claim shows (a) exposure without outcome,
# (b) outcome without exposure, or (c) a rival cause that explains the outcome.

options = {
    "A": {"exposure_no_outcome": True,  "outcome_no_exposure": False, "rival_cause": False,
          "note": "young Japanese women; population and age differ"},
    "B": {"exposure_no_outcome": False, "outcome_no_exposure": False, "rival_cause": True,
          "note": "names strain/infection as the root cause (rival cause, no direct link to exposure)"},
    "C": {"exposure_no_outcome": True,  "outcome_no_exposure": False, "rival_cause": False,
          "note": "sister shares household and habit, no arthritis (single case)"},
    "D": {"exposure_no_outcome": False, "outcome_no_exposure": True,  "rival_cause": True,
          "note": "arthritis in people who dress warmly; most are middle-aged or elderly (age as rival cause)"},
}

def undermines(opt):
    return opt["exposure_no_outcome"] or opt["outcome_no_exposure"] or opt["rival_cause"]

submitted = "D"
s = options[submitted]

print("Submitted answer:", submitted)
print("Content:", s["note"])
print("Breaks causal link (outcome without exposure):", s["outcome_no_exposure"])
print("Offers rival cause:", s["rival_cause"])

if undermines(s) and s["outcome_no_exposure"] and s["rival_cause"]:
    print("CHECK PASS: option D is a valid structural counterexample to the causal claim.")
else:
    print("CHECK FAIL: option D does not meet the counterexample criteria.")

undermining = [k for k, v in options.items() if undermines(v)]
print("Options with some undermining structure:", undermining)
print("UNSUPPORTED: ranking which option 'most' questions requires interpretive judgment; "
      "exact selection cannot be settled by computation alone.")
